claims.text: The rider's threshold burden of identity under POL-RD-08(a) is met: EV-TRIP-00510, EV-GPS-00510 and EV-FARE-00510 all carry trip_id TRP-00510 for rider RDR-20510 and driver DRV-20812, the trace opens at 2026-08-29T09:11:40 (the trip_record's started_at) and closes at 09:30:40 (its ended_at), and the ledger line was charged at 09:31:00 the same morning. There is no identifier mismatch to escalate on.

The POL-RD-01 establishment test passes on this trip's own trace. The governing field, gps_trace.trace_distance_km, is 8.8 km, against an optimal_distance_km of 6.2 km recorded on the trip_record at booking: an excess of 2.6 km. That is 41.9% of optimal, above the 20% limb, and 2.6 km in absolute terms, above the 0.8 km limb - both tests pass. The trip_record's actual_distance_km (8.8) is the rounded convenience copy of the same measurement, so nothing turns on which field is read, but the trace figure is the one the clause makes governing.

The trace needed to carry that finding is clean, so POL-RD-07 does not bite. The trace has 115 fixes at a 10 s sample interval with coverage_pct 100.0, gaps is empty, max_gap_sec is 0.0, and the admissibility pre-pass records status COMPLETE with weight_multiplier 1.0 and no issues. None of limbs (a) to (c) of POL-RD-07 fires - no gap over 90 s, no 500 m jump, no interval above 30 s - so the deviation may be established on this trace without independent corroboration.

No closure exoneration is available under POL-RD-03, and the record should say why. The only artifact that could carry it, EV-ADVIS-00510-01 (TRAFFIC_ADVISORY), is MISSING: it has no payload, admissibility status MISSING with weight_multiplier 0.0, and issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT - 'No advisory covers the optimal corridor in this window.' The absence is itself citable, and it means no advisory names any road, expressway segment or junction that the 6.2 km optimal route traverses, so there is no validity window to overlap and no closure to cap.

No rider-requested detour can be argued under POL-RD-04, because there is no chat_log content at all. EV-CHAT-00510 records message_count 0, messages as an empty array, first_message_at and last_message_at both null and truncated false. There is therefore no rider instruction timestamped before the vehicle left the optimal corridor or within 3 minutes after it, no waypoint_hint and no named road; the corroboration test cannot be run and the clause is unavailable, so the 2.6 km excess is not attributable to the rider.

No relocation re-quote applies under POL-RD-05. The trip_record shows pickup_amended_at and dropoff_amended_at both null, and amended_optimal_distance_km and amended_optimal_duration_min both null, with original_pickup and original_dropoff null as well. With no amendment timestamp there is nothing to re-run POL-RD-01 against and no stored amended optimal to substitute; the booked 6.2 km / 10.0 min optimal route stands as the baseline, and no pre-amendment or circling distance needs excluding.

The pooled baseline in POL-RD-12 is not in play: trip_record.vehicle_type is RYDE_X, not RYDE_POOL, and solo_optimal_distance_km is null. This was a single-rider trip, so the correct baseline is the 6.2 km optimal the platform computed at booking, and the whole 2.6 km excess counts against the driver rather than being absorbed as co-rider collection distance.

Once the rider has shown identity and a threshold-meeting excess, POL-RD-08 shifts the burden to the driver to point to a specific artifact and a specific clause, and the driver has not done so. The driver's own statement concedes the route: 'I missed the exit, it happens. I looped back right away.' That is a party admission that the exit was missed and the vehicle left the optimal corridor; his remaining sentence, that 'the fare is calculated by the app, not me', invokes no clause and cites no artifact. A general assertion unsupported by an artifact carries no weight under POL-RD-08, and the empty chat log cannot supply the rider instruction POL-RD-04 would require.

The money on this trip is governed by POL-RD-11, not POL-RD-02. fare_breakdown.fare_model is UPFRONT_QUOTE and quoted_fare_sgd is non-null at 15.80, so the distance and time charges were fixed at booking and no distance-or-time refund is sought; the rider is not asking the driver to pay for the detour out of the metered lines. What the rider is owed is limb (a): charged_total of 25.80 exceeds the 15.80 quote, and the only lines that may be added to the quote before comparing are pass-through and statutory lines under POL-RD-09 - ERP and tolls actually crossed (0.00 here), a properly chargeable airport surcharge (none: this trip runs Toa Payoh to Kallang and does not originate at an airport), and waiting_time_fee (0.00). The refund is therefore 25.80 - 15.80 = 10.00, which is exactly the charged_over_quote figure the fare artifact publishes, rounded up to the nearest SGD 0.05 = 10.00.

Nothing in the ERP and pass-through layer either adds to or nets down that figure. EV-FARE-00510 shows erp_gantries as an empty array, tolls_erp 0.00, airport_surcharge 0.00, waiting_time_fee 0.00 and surge_multiplier 1.0 read from the fare_breakdown, with the derived ERP totals on-optimal 0.00 and off-optimal 0.00. There is consequently no off-route ERP charge to refund separately under POL-RD-09(2), no rider-caused detour under POL-RD-09(3) to withhold one, and no risk of the POL-RD-09(1) double-count, because the 10.00 the rider seeks is a quote overcharge on the fare lines and not a gantry correction. The rider's complaint - that the app quietly charged more than the fixed price and the passenger had to ask to get it back - is precisely the 10.00 this clause measures.

This case is ripe for a monetary ruling and none of the POL-RD-10 escalation triggers fires. The trip identifiers on trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown all match (no (2)); the trace is not impaired under POL-RD-07(a)-(c) and is in any event corroborated by the driver's admission of a missed exit (no (3)); no exculpatory clause is invoked against a missing artifact, because no closure, detour or amendment is asserted at all (no (5)); the computed refund of 10.00 is far below SGD 150.00 and below charged_total (no (6)); and there is no unmatched charge line, the ERP, toll, surcharge and waiting lines all being zero (no (8)). Holding the disputed amount for a human reviewer would add nothing a reading of these artifacts has not already settled.

On weight, POL-GEN-02 is satisfied for the rider's case: every artifact carrying the facts the rider relies on - EV-FARE-00510 for the quoted-versus-charged comparison, EV-GPS-00510 for the trace, EV-TRIP-00510 for the booking optimal - is COMPLETE with weight_multiplier 1.0 and no issue codes. The only artifact below 1.0 in the bundle is the MISSING traffic advisory at weight 0.0, which carries no fact and is relied on here solely for its absence; it does not carry the deciding fact, so it does not cap confidence and does not force an escalation under POL-RD-10(1).

claims.text: TRP-00510 is an upfront-quoted trip: fare_breakdown.fare_model is UPFRONT_QUOTE with a non-null quoted_fare_sgd of 15.80, so the distance and time lines were fixed at booking and POL-RD-02 does not run. The 6.2 km optimal route, the 8.8 km trace and the 2.6 km / 41.9% excess therefore settle nothing on the money — under POL-RD-11 no distance-or-time refund is available to the rider however large the excess, because the rider is already whole on those lines and the driver's unrecovered cost on a detour of this kind is not recoverable from the rider under this clause.

The rider's remedies under POL-RD-11 are confined to the amount by which charged_total exceeds quoted_fare_sgd plus the pass-through and statutory lines properly chargeable under POL-RD-09. On this ledger that is 25.80 less 15.80 less 0.00, which is exactly the 10.00 the ledger itself publishes as derived.money.charged_over_quote. The contested figure of 25.80 cannot be the measure of this dispute: the recoverable sum cannot exceed 10.00, and the remaining 15.80 of the present charge stands.

The excess is 2.6 km over a 6.2 km optimal route, 41.9%. That clears the POL-RD-01 establishment gate (above 20% and above 0.8 km absolute) but falls under both materiality gates — 50% and 8.0 km — so this is not a MATERIAL deviation. The evidence is not finely balanced either: the trace is complete and unimpaired at 100% coverage. POL-RD-06 is therefore not engaged, and none of its three effects can attach: no rider-favourable resolution of a balanced record, no FULL_REFUND uplift of charged_total, and no driver-conduct referral.

Even if POL-RD-06 were consulted, the pattern test fails on both limbs: driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0, and 0 divided by driver_profile.completed_trips_90d of 250 is 0.00 — below the 3-flag threshold and below the 0.05 ratio threshold. No repeat-deviation pattern is established, so no POL-RD-06 effect fires and no conduct referral is available; these are the only two driver_profile fields POL-RD-06 permits to be read for that test.

POL-RD-09 adds nothing on this trip. erp_gantries is empty and tolls_erp is 0.00; airport_surcharge is 0.00 on a trip that neither originates nor ends at Changi or Seletar; waiting_time_fee is 0.00 and promo_discount is 0.00. There is no phantom gantry, no off-route ERP and no wrongly applied surcharge, so no standalone pass-through correction under POL-RD-09(4) exists to be stacked on top of the over-quote figure, and the 10.00 over-quote is the ceiling of this dispute.

The route finding rests on a clean trace, not a gap-ridden one: EV-GPS-00510 samples at 10-second intervals against an expected 10 seconds, covers 100% of the trip, records no gaps and a maximum inter-fix gap of 0.0 seconds, and carries admissibility COMPLETE with no issue codes and weight 1.0. POL-RD-07's impairment limbs (a) to (c) are not met, so nothing on this trace requires independent corroboration and the driver's account of a single missed exit promptly corrected is unrebutted on the record.

This case is confined to TRP-00510. The rider's assertion that the app 'quietly charges more' a few times over points to no other trip and cites no evidence ID, and no artifact in the pool covers any trip but this one — the trip record carries a single trip_id and the trip's chat export carries zero messages. The profiles on both sides are credibility weighting only under POL-GEN-01 and cannot establish a systemic billing practice or any fact about this trip.

ruling.explanation: TRP-00510 was booked on an upfront fixed price, and that is what decides the money. EV-FARE-00510 records fare_model UPFRONT_QUOTE with a quoted fare of SGD 15.80, but the amount actually charged was SGD 25.80. Under POL-RD-11 the distance and time charges on an upfront-quoted trip are fixed at booking, so the driver's missed exit costs the rider nothing on those lines and POL-RD-02 does not run: however large the excess, there is no distance-or-time refund. The rider's remedy is the amount by which the charge exceeded the quote — 25.80 minus 15.80 = 10.00 — because no pass-through or statutory line may be added to the quote: ERP is 0.00, tolls are 0.00, the airport surcharge is 0.00 (this trip runs Toa Payoh to Kallang and neither starts nor ends at an airport), and the waiting-time fee is 0.00. The refund is therefore SGD 10.00, rounded up to the nearest SGD 0.05, and the remaining SGD 15.80 of the charge is the fixed price and stands. This is a PARTIAL_REFUND: SGD 10.00 of the SGD 25.80 contested is returned. The rider's wider point — that the app charged more than the fixed price and the passenger had to ask — is exactly the SGD 10.00 refunded here. On the route itself: the GPS trace (EV-GPS-00510) gives 8.8 km against the booked 6.2 km optimal, an excess of 2.6 km or 41.9%, which clears the POL-RD-01 establishment gate (above 20% and above 0.8 km) but falls below both materiality gates (50% and 8.0 km). The deviation is therefore established but not MATERIAL, so POL-RD-06 is not engaged and no driver-conduct referral follows; and the driver profile shows deviation_flags_90d 0 over 250 completed trips in 90 days, so no repeat-deviation pattern exists in any event. The driver's statement that he missed the exit is accepted as an admission that the corridor was left — but on an upfront-quoted trip a faultless or a faulty detour makes no difference to the distance and time lines, so it changes no figure. No exculpation clause is available on this record: EV-ADVIS-00510-01 (TRAFFIC_ADVISORY) is a MISSING artifact at weight 0.0 with issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, so no closure is asserted or exonerated under POL-RD-03; EV-CHAT-00510 carries zero messages and no waypoint_hint, so no rider-requested detour can be run under POL-RD-04; the trip record shows no pickup or dropoff amendment, so POL-RD-05 does not apply; and the vehicle is RYDE_X with solo_optimal_distance_km null, so POL-RD-12 is out. The trace is clean for policy purposes — 115 fixes at a 10-second interval, 100% coverage, no gaps, max gap 0.0 seconds, weight 1.0 — so POL-RD-07 does not bite and no independent corroboration is needed. The only artifact below weight 1.0 in the bundle is the missing advisory, which carries no fact (its absence alone is citable) and so does not cap confidence; the deciding fact, the fare overage, is carried by EV-FARE-00510 at weight 1.0, and confidence is 0.95, above the 0.70 floor. No POL-RD-10 escalation trigger fires and no clause produces a referral.

This was an upfront-quoted trip: EV-FARE-00510 carries fare_model UPFRONT_QUOTE, so the distance and time lines were fixed at booking and no distance-or-time refund runs under POL-RD-02 however long the detour. The figures I read off EV-FARE-00510 are quoted_fare_sgd 15.80 and charged_total 25.80, with every pass-through line nil (tolls_erp 0.00, airport_surcharge 0.00, waiting_time_fee 0.00, erp_gantries empty). Under POL-RD-11(a) the amount by which the charge exceeds the quote plus properly chargeable pass-through lines is refunded in full: 25.80 - 15.80 - 0.00 = 10.00, which is exactly the ledger's own published charged_over_quote figure. Rounded up to the nearest SGD 0.05 that is SGD 10.00, and the remaining 15.80 of the present charge stands. The disputed figure of 25.80 is therefore not the measure of the case; the recoverable sum is 10.00. The deviation is established on this trip: EV-GPS-00510 (COMPLETE, weight 1.0, 115 fixes at a 10 s cadence, no gaps, coverage 100%) traces 8.8 km against the 6.2 km booking optimal, an excess of 2.6 km / 41.9%. That clears POL-RD-01's 20% and 0.8 km gates but not the 50% or 8.0 km materiality gates, so POL-RD-06 is not engaged; had it been consulted, driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against completed_trips_90d 250, so no repeat-deviation pattern exists either. The driver's statement that he missed the exit and looped back is accepted as an admission against interest and corroborates the deviation, but it moves no money and produces no referral. No exculpatory or rider-caused excuse applies: POL-RD-03 has no traffic advisory (EV-ADVIS-00510-01 is MISSING at weight 0.0 with issue MISSING_ARTIFACT - its absence is citable but carries no fact and does not cap confidence); POL-RD-04 finds no chat content at all (EV-CHAT-00510 has zero messages, no waypoint_hint, no named road); POL-RD-05 finds no amended pickup or dropoff; POL-RD-12 finds vehicle_type RYDE_X, not RYDE_POOL. The ERP and pass-through layer is empty, so POL-RD-09 adds nothing and no billing-integrity correction or referral arises. No POL-RD-10 escalation trigger fires: identifiers match, the trace is unimpaired, timestamps agree, no clause is invoked against a missing artifact, the refund is well below 150.00 and below charged_total, and no charge line lacks a counterpart. My confidence rests on the deciding fact - the over-quote - carried by EV-FARE-00510 at weight 1.0.

ruling.explanation:
Both of you are reading the same trip, and on the money you largely agree. Here is the ruling.

The route fact. The GPS trace EV-GPS-00510 records 8.8 km driven against the 6.2 km optimal route stored on the trip record EV-TRIP-00510 at booking — an excess of 2.6 km, or 41.9%. That clears POL-RD-01's establishment gate (more than 20% of optimal AND more than 0.8 km absolute), so a deviation is established. It does not reach the materiality gates (50% or 8.0 km), so POL-RD-06 is not engaged: the driver profile EV-DPROF-00510 shows deviation_flags_90d of 0 over 250 completed trips in 90 days, so no repeat pattern exists, no FULL_REFUND uplift attaches and no driver-conduct referral is made. The trace is clean (115 fixes, 10-second cadence, no gaps, 100% coverage, weight 1.0), so POL-RD-07 imposes no corroboration requirement.

The money. TRP-00510 was booked on an upfront quote. EV-FARE-00510 shows fare_model UPFRONT_QUOTE and quoted_fare_sgd 15.80, so POL-RD-02 does not run and no distance-or-time refund is available for the detour — the rider was already protected on those lines at booking, and the driver's unrecovered cost on this kind of detour is not recoverable from the rider. What the rider is owed is the amount by which the charged total exceeded the quote, under POL-RD-11: charged_total 25.80 less quoted_fare 15.80, with no ERP or tolls crossed (0.00), no airport surcharge (this trip runs Toa Payoh to Kallang and did not originate at an airport) and no waiting fee (0.00). That is 10.00 — the figure EV-FARE-00510 itself publishes as charged_over_quote. Rounded up to the nearest SGD 0.05, the refund is SGD 10.00. The remaining 15.80 of the charge stands.

The driver's statement — 'I missed the exit, it happens. I looped back right away.' — is an admission that the exit was missed and is accepted as such, but it does not change the amount: on an upfront-quoted trip a detour costs the rider nothing on the distance and time lines, and the 10.00 is the quote overcharge, refunded whether or not the driver was at fault. The rider's wider complaint that the app 'quietly charges more' over several trips is confined to TRP-00510; no artifact in the pool covers any other trip, and the profiles on both sides are credibility weighting only under POL-GEN-01.

No other clause moves the figure. There is no traffic advisory (EV-ADVIS-00510-01 is MISSING, weight 0.0, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT), no chat content at all (EV-CHAT-00510 has zero messages, so POL-RD-04's waypoint test cannot be run and the clause is unavailable), no pickup or dropoff amendment (so POL-RD-05 does not apply), and vehicle_type is RYDE_X rather than RYDE_POOL (so POL-RD-12's pooled baseline is not in play). ERP, tolls and surcharges are all 0.00, so POL-RD-09 adds nothing in either direction — there is no off-route gantry and no billing-integrity correction to stack on top.

Escalation. None of the POL-RD-10 triggers fires. The trip identifiers match across trip record, trace and ledger (TRP-00510); the trace is not impaired under POL-RD-07(a)–(c); the computed refund is far below the SGD 150.00 ceiling and below the charged total; no exculpatory clause is asserted against a missing artifact (the absent advisory exonerates nothing and is relied on only for its absence); and no charge line is unmatched. The confidence cap is 1.0, because the deciding facts sit on weight-1.0 artifacts — EV-FARE-00510 for the quote-versus-charge comparison, EV-GPS-00510 and EV-TRIP-00510 for the route measurement — and confidence is set at 0.95.

Driver compensation. None is due: the ledger bills 8.8 km and the trace records 8.8 km, so there is no unbilled-kilometre shortfall for POL-RD-04's compensation limb, and no other clause produces a payment to the driver.

Under POL-RD-11 the distance and time lines were fixed at booking, so POL-RD-02 does not run and the rider cannot recover on the detour however long it was; the rider is already whole on those lines. What the rider can recover is the over-quote: the amount by which the charge exceeds the quote plus the pass-through and statutory lines properly chargeable under POL-RD-09. That is 25.80 - 15.80 = 10.00, with nothing to add (ERP 0.00, tolls 0.00, airport surcharge 0.00 on a Toa Payoh-to-Kallang trip that neither starts nor ends at an airport, waiting fee 0.00). The refund is SGD 10.00, already a multiple of SGD 0.05. The remaining SGD 15.80 of the charge stands, so this is a partial refund, not a full one.
ruling.explanation_2: On the route itself: the GPS trace (EV-GPS-00510, weight 1.0, 115 fixes at a 10-second cadence, no gaps, 100% coverage) shows 8.8 km driven against the 6.2 km optimal recorded at booking — an excess of 2.6 km, 41.9%. That passes both POL-RD-01 establishment limbs (above 20% and above 0.8 km) but is below both materiality gates (50% and 8.0 km), so POL-RD-06 is not engaged and no driver-conduct referral issues. The trace is clean, so POL-RD-07's impairment limbs do not fire and nothing needed independent corroboration.
ruling.explanation_3: Nothing else moves the figure. The only artifact that could have exonerated the detour, the traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-00510-01, is MISSING at weight 0.0 with issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, so there is no closure to invoke under POL-RD-03; the chat export (EV-CHAT-00510) carries zero messages, so there is no rider-requested detour under POL-RD-04; and no pickup or dropoff amendment is recorded, so POL-RD-05 cannot be run. The driver's statement that he 'missed the exit' is an admission that the corridor was left, but under upfront pricing the cost of that detour falls on the driver and not on the rider, so it changes no amount.
ruling.explanation_4: The rider's wider complaint that the app 'quietly charges more' a few times points to no other trip and cites no artifact, and the profiles on both sides are credibility weighting only under POL-GEN-01 — they cannot establish a systemic billing practice. No escalation trigger under POL-RD-10 fires: identifiers match across the three instruments, the trace is unimpaired, the refund is far below the SGD 150 ceiling, and every charge line has a counterpart in the trip record and trace. Confidence is 0.90; the deciding fact, the SGD 10.00 over-quote, is carried by EV-FARE-00510 at weight 1.0.

ledger.claim: The rider's threshold burden of identity under POL-RD-08(a) is met: EV-TRIP-00510, EV-GPS-00510 and EV-FARE-00510 all carry trip_id TRP-00510 for rider RDR-20510 and driver DRV-20812, the trace opens at 2026-08-29T09:11:40 (the trip_record's started_at) and closes at 09:30:40 (its ended_at), and the ledger line was charged at 09:31:00 the same morning. There is no identifier mismatch to escalate on.

The POL-RD-01 establishment test passes on this trip's own trace. The governing field, gps_trace.trace_distance_km, is 8.8 km, against an optimal_distance_km of 6.2 km recorded on the trip_record at booking: an excess of 2.6 km. That is 41.9% of optimal, above the 20% limb, and 2.6 km in absolute terms, above the 0.8 km limb - both tests pass. The trip_record's actual_distance_km (8.8) is the rounded convenience copy of the same measurement, so nothing turns on which field is read, but the trace figure is the one the clause makes governing.

The trace needed to carry that finding is clean, so POL-RD-07 does not bite. The trace has 115 fixes at a 10 s sample interval with coverage_pct 100.0, gaps is empty, max_gap_sec is 0.0, and the admissibility pre-pass records status COMPLETE with weight_multiplier 1.0 and no issues. None of limbs (a) to (c) of POL-RD-07 fires - no gap over 90 s, no 500 m jump, no interval above 30 s - so the deviation may be established on this trace without independent corroboration.

No closure exoneration is available under POL-RD-03, and the record should say why. The only artifact that could carry it, EV-ADVIS-00510-01 (TRAFFIC_ADVISORY), is MISSING: it has no payload, admissibility status MISSING with weight_multiplier 0.0, and issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT - 'No advisory covers the optimal corridor in this window.' The absence is itself citable, and it means no advisory names any road, expressway segment or junction that the 6.2 km optimal route traverses, so there is no validity window to overlap and no closure to cap.

No rider-requested detour can be argued under POL-RD-04, because there is no chat_log content at all. EV-CHAT-00510 records message_count 0, messages as an empty array, first_message_at and last_message_at both null and truncated false. There is therefore no rider instruction timestamped before the vehicle left the optimal corridor or within 3 minutes after it, no waypoint_hint and no named road; the corroboration test cannot be run and the clause is unavailable, so the 2.6 km excess is not attributable to the rider.

No relocation re-quote applies under POL-RD-05. The trip_record shows pickup_amended_at and dropoff_amended_at both null, and amended_optimal_distance_km and amended_optimal_duration_min both null, with original_pickup and original_dropoff null as well. With no amendment timestamp there is nothing to re-run POL-RD-01 against and no stored amended optimal to substitute; the booked 6.2 km / 10.0 min optimal route stands as the baseline, and no pre-amendment or circling distance needs excluding.

The pooled baseline in POL-RD-12 is not in play: trip_record.vehicle_type is RYDE_X, not RYDE_POOL, and solo_optimal_distance_km is null. This was a single-rider trip, so the correct baseline is the 6.2 km optimal the platform computed at booking, and the whole 2.6 km excess counts against the driver rather than being absorbed as co-rider collection distance.

Once the rider has shown identity and a threshold-meeting excess, POL-RD-08 shifts the burden to the driver to point to a specific artifact and a specific clause, and the driver has not done so. The driver's own statement concedes the route: 'I missed the exit, it happens. I looped back right away.' That is a party admission that the exit was missed and the vehicle left the optimal corridor; his remaining sentence, that 'the fare is calculated by the app, not me', invokes no clause and cites no artifact. A general assertion unsupported by an artifact carries no weight under POL-RD-08, and the empty chat log cannot supply the rider instruction POL-RD-04 would require.

The money on this trip is governed by POL-RD-11, not POL-RD-02. fare_breakdown.fare_model is UPFRONT_QUOTE and quoted_fare_sgd is non-null at 15.80, so the distance and time charges were fixed at booking and no distance-or-time refund is sought; the rider is not asking the driver to pay for the detour out of the metered lines. What the rider is owed is limb (a): charged_total of 25.80 exceeds the 15.80 quote, and the only lines that may be added to the quote before comparing are pass-through and statutory lines under POL-RD-09 - ERP and tolls actually crossed (0.00 here), a properly chargeable airport surcharge (none: this trip runs Toa Payoh to Kallang and does not originate at an airport), and waiting_time_fee (0.00). The refund is therefore 25.80 - 15.80 = 10.00, which is exactly the charged_over_quote figure the fare artifact publishes, rounded up to the nearest SGD 0.05 = 10.00.

Nothing in the ERP and pass-through layer either adds to or nets down that figure. EV-FARE-00510 shows erp_gantries as an empty array, tolls_erp 0.00, airport_surcharge 0.00, waiting_time_fee 0.00 and surge_multiplier 1.0 read from the fare_breakdown, with the derived ERP totals on-optimal 0.00 and off-optimal 0.00. There is consequently no off-route ERP charge to refund separately under POL-RD-09(2), no rider-caused detour under POL-RD-09(3) to withhold one, and no risk of the POL-RD-09(1) double-count, because the 10.00 the rider seeks is a quote overcharge on the fare lines and not a gantry correction. The rider's complaint - that the app quietly charged more than the fixed price and the passenger had to ask to get it back - is precisely the 10.00 this clause measures.

This case is ripe for a monetary ruling and none of the POL-RD-10 escalation triggers fires. The trip identifiers on trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown all match (no (2)); the trace is not impaired under POL-RD-07(a)-(c) and is in any event corroborated by the driver's admission of a missed exit (no (3)); no exculpatory clause is invoked against a missing artifact, because no closure, detour or amendment is asserted at all (no (5)); the computed refund of 10.00 is far below SGD 150.00 and below charged_total (no (6)); and there is no unmatched charge line, the ERP, toll, surcharge and waiting lines all being zero (no (8)). Holding the disputed amount for a human reviewer would add nothing a reading of these artifacts has not already settled.

On weight, POL-GEN-02 is satisfied for the rider's case: every artifact carrying the facts the rider relies on - EV-FARE-00510 for the quoted-versus-charged comparison, EV-GPS-00510 for the trace, EV-TRIP-00510 for the booking optimal - is COMPLETE with weight_multiplier 1.0 and no issue codes. The only artifact below 1.0 in the bundle is the MISSING traffic advisory at weight 0.0, which carries no fact and is relied on here solely for its absence; it does not carry the deciding fact, so it does not cap confidence and does not force an escalation under POL-RD-10(1).

The 6.2 km optimal route, the 8.8 km trace and the 2.6 km / 41.9% excess therefore settle nothing on the money — under POL-RD-11 no distance-or-time refund is available to the rider however large the excess, because the rider is already whole on those lines and the driver's unrecovered cost on a detour of this kind is not recoverable from the rider under this clause.

The rider's remedies under POL-RD-11 are confined to the amount by which charged_total exceeds quoted_fare_sgd plus the pass-through and statutory lines properly chargeable under POL-RD-09. On this ledger that is 25.80 less 15.80 less 0.00, which is exactly the 10.00 the ledger itself publishes as derived.money.charged_over_quote. The contested figure of 25.80 cannot be the measure of this dispute: the recoverable sum cannot exceed 10.00, and the remaining 15.80 of the present charge stands.

The excess is 2.6 km over a 6.2 km optimal route, 41.9%. That clears the POL-RD-01 establishment gate (above 20% and above 0.8 km absolute) but falls under both materiality gates — 50% and 8.0 km — so this is not a MATERIAL deviation. The evidence is not finely balanced either: the trace is complete and unimpaired at 100% coverage. POL-RD-06 is therefore not engaged, and none of its three effects can attach: no rider-favourable resolution of a balanced record, no FULL_REFUND uplift of charged_total, and no driver-conduct referral.

Even if POL-RD-06 were consulted, the pattern test fails on both limbs: driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0, and 0 divided by driver_profile.completed_trips_90d of 250 is 0.00 — below the 3-flag threshold and below the 0.05 ratio threshold. No repeat-deviation pattern is established, so no POL-RD-06 effect fires and no conduct referral is available; these are the only two driver_profile fields POL-RD-06 permits to be read for that test.

POL-RD-09 adds nothing on this trip. erp_gantries is empty and tolls_erp is 0.00; airport_surcharge is 0.00 on a trip that neither originates nor ends at Changi or Seletar; waiting_time_fee is 0.00 and promo_discount is 0.00. There is no phantom gantry, no off-route ERP and no wrongly applied surcharge, so no standalone pass-through correction under POL-RD-09(4) exists to be stacked on top of the over-quote figure, and the 10.00 over-quote is the ceiling of this dispute.

The route finding rests on a clean trace, not a gap-ridden one: EV-GPS-00510 samples at 10-second intervals against an expected 10 seconds, covers 100% of the trip, records no gaps and a maximum inter-fix gap of 0.0 seconds, and carries admissibility COMPLETE with no issue codes and weight 1.0. POL-RD-07's impairment limbs (a) to (c) are not met, so nothing on this trace requires independent corroboration and the driver's account of a single missed exit promptly corrected is unrebutted on the record.

This case is confined to TRP-00510. The rider's assertion that the app 'quietly charges more' a few times over points to no other trip and cites no evidence ID, and no artifact in the pool covers any trip but this one — the trip record carries a single trip_id and the trip's chat export carries zero messages. The profiles on both sides are credibility weighting only under POL-GEN-01 and cannot establish a systemic billing practice or any fact about this trip.
